subsystems.name: Sensor nodes
subsystems.role: measure the local environment — temperature, humidity, pressure, motion, gases, sound or light.

subsystems.name: Power and harvesting
subsystems.role: let a node run for years without a battery change.
parts: thin-film solar cell or vibration/thermal harvester

subsystems.name: Communications and mesh
subsystems.role: move readings hop-by-hop to the nearest gateway.

subsystems.name: Deployment layer
subsystems.role: gets nodes into position and keeps them there.

subsystems.name: Backhaul and gateways
subsystems.role: collects local mesh traffic and forwards it onward.

subsystems.name: Data and compute layer
subsystems.role: turns billions of noisy readings into usable information.

buildSteps.title: Design the sensing element
buildSteps.detail: Each sensor type is patterned on a silicon wafer by photolithography and etching, so that a microscopic beam, membrane or cavity responds to one physical quantity.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the electronics
buildSteps.detail: The radio, processor and analogue circuits are made as a complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor chip, then the sensor die and the circuit die are bonded together, giving a device a few millimetres across.

buildSteps.title: Add power
buildSteps.detail: A photovoltaic or vibration harvester and a tiny storage cell are attached, sized so the node can transmit a reading every few minutes indefinitely.

buildSteps.title: Package and harden
buildSteps.detail: The node is encapsulated against water, salt, dust and ultraviolet light, ideally in a coating that will break down safely if it is never recovered.

buildSteps.title: Mass-produce
buildSteps.detail: Wafers are diced and packaged on highly automated lines, or flexible versions are printed roll-to-roll, to push unit cost low enough that losing nodes is acceptable.

buildSteps.title: Disperse or place
buildSteps.detail: Large numbers would be released from aircraft, balloons or drones over the target region, or installed by hand and by marine platforms where recovery is possible.

buildSteps.title: Form the mesh
buildSteps.detail: On power-up each node discovers its neighbours, agrees a shared clock and builds routing paths so that data hops toward a gateway without any central controller.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate in place
buildSteps.detail: Nodes are cross-checked against reference instruments and against each other, because cheap sensors drift and a whole mesh of biased readings is worse than none.

buildSteps.title: Aggregate and interpret
buildSteps.detail: Gateways relay the traffic by satellite or fixed link to data centres, where readings are fused with weather, satellite and model data to produce usable maps and forecasts.

prerequisites.why: the sensing elements themselves are already mass-produced in phones and cars.
harvesters work in bright, vibrating places but fail in darkness, calm or cold.
protocols that let thousands of nodes cooperate already exist; millions per network do not.
remote regions have no ground infrastructure, so data must leave by satellite or high-altitude platform.
routing, addressing and synchronisation are unproven for trillion-node, constantly failing networks.
scattering hardware across land, ocean and atmosphere is pollution unless the materials biodegrade cleanly.

pathway.milestone: regional networks of thousands of fixed and drifting sensors — weather stations, air-quality monitors and ocean profiling floats such as the Argo array
pathway.unlocks: real-time environmental monitoring over well-instrumented regions.

pathway.milestone: low-power wide-area and satellite IoT connect millions of cheap nodes, mostly in agriculture, logistics and industry
pathway.unlocks: commodity hardware, cheap radios and battery-life lessons that a planetary mesh would need.

pathway.milestone: millimetre-scale nodes with on-board harvesting demonstrated in laboratory and small-area trials, in the lineage of the long-running 'smart dust' research idea
pathway.unlocks: deployments where wires and batteries are impossible.

pathway.milestone: self-organising, largely biodegradable meshes over remote land, ice and ocean, with satellite backhaul
pathway.unlocks: near-continuous observation of the whole planet's surface and lower atmosphere.

pathway.milestone: truly continuous coverage of every square metre, if ever achievable and acceptable
pathway.unlocks: environmental models constrained by direct measurement everywhere — at a cost in materials, energy and surveillance risk that may not be worth paying.
